title: Outer enumeration invariant
statement:
Let $E,B$ be natural numbers, let $\mathcal O:\{0,1,2,3\}	imes\{0,1\}^*	o\{0,1\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\operatorname{Kont}:\mathbb N	o\mathrm{Prop}$, and let $\sigma$ be a counting state. For $u,v\in\mathbb N$, let $R(u,v)$ and $I(u)$ denote respectively the truth of the type-$3$ query encoding $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ and the type-$1$ query encoding $(x,u,\sigma.s)$, and let $\operatorname{Mem}_j(t)$ mean that some $I$-witness below $\sigma.K$ reaches $t$ in at most $j$ steps of $R$. Suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$, $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.v\le\sigma.K$, $\sigma.c\le\sigma.v$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$. Assume that for every $c'\le\sigma.K$, if the outer recursive condition holds from position $\sigma.v$, count $\sigma.c$, and depth $\sigma.K-\sigma.v$, with terminal condition $c=c'$, then the stage-end machine initialized with $v=K,c=c'$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $\operatorname{Kont}(c')$ holds. The outer condition uses first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_{i1}(t)\land
eg\operatorname{AccO}(t)$ and second predicate given by the inner recursive condition of depth $K$, starting at position and count zero, with first predicate $\operatorname{Mem}_i(u)\land u
e t\land
eg R(u,t)$, second predicate always true, and terminal condition count $\sigma.cp$. Then the machine initialized at the outer-enumeration test state with registers $\sigma$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when the outer recursive condition holds with terminal predicate $\operatorname{Kont}$.

Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle,
let $\operatorname{Kont}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathrm{Prop}$, and let $\sigma$ be a register
state with every register at most $B$. Write $R(u,v)$ for the truth of the oracle's
type-$3$ query on $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$ and $I(u)$ for the truth of its type-$1$ query on
$(x,u,\sigma.s)$; let $\operatorname{Mem}_j(t)$ mean that some $I$-code below $\sigma.K$
reaches $t$ in at most $j$ steps of $R$. Use the recursive predicate $\operatorname{GS}$
that at each step either satisfies its first predicate and increments the count, or
satisfies its second predicate and leaves the count unchanged, with its terminal
predicate imposed at depth zero. Suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.v\le\sigma.K$,
$\sigma.c\le\sigma.v$, and $\sigma.g=\sigma.cur=\sigma.stp=\sigma.u=\sigma.cnt=0$.
Assume for every $c'\le\sigma.K$ that the outer recursive condition starting at
$t=\sigma.v$, count $c=\sigma.c$, and depth $\sigma.K-\sigma.v$ implies that the machine
at the stage-end state with $v=K,c=c'$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts
exactly when $\operatorname{Kont}(c')$ holds. Here the first outer predicate is
$\operatorname{Mem}_{i1}(t)$ and oracle nonacceptance at $t$; its second predicate is
the inner recursive count condition over all $u<K$, with depth $K$, start $t=0$, count
$0$, and terminal count $\sigma.cp$. Then the machine initialized at the
outer-enumeration test with state $\sigma$ terminates within that bound and accepts
exactly when this outer recursive condition holds with terminal predicate
$\operatorname{Kont}$.
